title: Anansi Buys the Sky God's Stories
text:
Long ago all stories belonged to Nyame, the sky god. Anansi the spider went up to him and asked to buy them. Nyame laughed: great and wealthy towns had tried and failed. But he named a price. Anansi must bring him the python, the leopard, the hornets and Mmoatia, the fairy. Anansi agreed.

For the python, Anansi cut a palm branch and walked past the python's home arguing loudly with his wife about whether the python was longer than the branch. The python, overhearing, offered to settle it and stretched out along the branch. Anansi said he would tie him to it to measure him properly, and tied him fast.

For the hornets, he filled a gourd with water, poured some over their nest and the rest over himself, and called out that it was raining. He invited them to shelter in an empty gourd, and when they flew in, he plugged it.

For the leopard, he dug a pit across its path and covered it. The leopard fell in, and Anansi caught it. For Mmoatia, he carved a doll, covered it with sticky gum and set a dish of mashed yams before it. The fairy ate the yams, and when the doll did not answer her thanks, she struck it and stuck fast.

Anansi carried all four to Nyame, who kept his word. From that day, the stories have been called Anansi's stories.
lesson: When you lack strength, study each obstacle separately and use its own habits against it. A different tactic for each problem beats one blunt approach.
people: Kwaku Anansi, Nyame the sky god, the python, the leopard, the hornets, Mmoatia
caveat: The tale exists in many versions, and the details of how each creature is caught differ between tellers.
